# Findings report

**Authors:** Omoding Isaac (Data Scientist, Ministry of Health), Echodu Moses (co-investigator, Uganda Cancer Institute) Bob Tumushime (Data Scientist, Uganda Bureau of Statistics), Noah Okiror and Daniel Baguma (Malaria Consortium)

**Working title:** *Survival Label Inconsistencies and Machine Learning Evaluation in Lung Cancer: A Source-Linked Reanalysis of the MMIST-LUNG Benchmark*

**Status:** complete analysis of public data, run 2026-11-05 under protocol v1.1. Not peer reviewed. All numbers are regenerated by `python -m src.run_analysis` and stored in `outputs/tables/`.

## Verdict: CONDITIONAL GO

**The label audit is the main result, and it is solid.** The released 12-month label in MMIST-LUNG is reproduced exactly by two rules with opposite polarity, and patients whose 12-month status is unknowable are labelled survivors. This is deterministic and needs no statistical assumption.

**The consequences for machine learning are real but uneven:**

| Claim | Strength |
|---|---|
| Labels reverse which cohort looks higher-risk, and models learn the reversal | Strong (direct counts; post-hoc mechanism analysis) |
| Training on source-derived labels improves true-label AUROC by about 0.05 | Moderate to strong (patient-level CIs exclude 0 for both models; post-hoc) |
| Label set changes the standing of the 15-feature models against a stage-only model | Moderate (interaction CIs exclude 0; post-hoc; one lower bound is 0.001) |
| Evaluation labels alone change AUROC for fixed predictions (**the pre-specified primary contrast**) | **Weak**: small, CI narrowly excludes 0, not robust across sensitivity analyses |

The evidence supports a **focused short article** of the technical-correspondence or benchmark-audit type. It does not support a full original article claiming a general phenomenon, and it does not show that the published MMIST-LUNG numbers are wrong by any specific amount.

The working title is supported. A more specific alternative, if a venue prefers one: *"Cohort-specific label inversion in a public multimodal lung cancer benchmark: a source-linked audit and its consequences for model evaluation."*

## Update: protocol v2 (replication and confirmatory tests)

Protocol v2 was committed publicly (commit `f3d3e14`) before any MMIST-ccRCC value or new model result was examined.

| Test | Pre-specified as | Result |
|---|---|---|
| C1: inversion in MMIST-ccRCC? | Confirmatory, with a fixed decision rule | **No inversion.** Recorded deaths agree 30/31 (CPTAC) and 169/169 (TCGA); 1 of 580 checkable labels contradicted |
| C2: training-label effect on MMIST-LUNG, refit bootstrap | Confirmatory | **Confirmed.** ψ_B +0.049 (95% CI +0.008 to +0.091), one-sided p = 0.010, Holm p = 0.010 |
| C3: training-label effect on MMIST-ccRCC | Confirmatory, if at least 20 contradictions | Not applicable (1 contradiction) |
| S4: training-label effect, XGBoost / MLP | Secondary | XGBoost +0.051 (−0.002 to +0.093), borderline; MLP +0.028 (−0.093 to +0.101), inconclusive |

**Exploratory findings in MMIST-ccRCC:**

- **Forced outcomes:** 38 CPTAC patients (20.1%) have unknown 12-month status. 20 were labelled survivors and 18 were labelled deaths.
- **The 18 deaths cannot be verified:** 17 have vital status "Not Reported" with no follow-up, 1 has a negative death time, and none appears in LinkedOmics.
- **Shortcut:** all 18 patients with missing pathological stage are labelled deaths, and 4 of the 16 deaths in the released test set have missing stage.
- **Metric inflation:** including unknown-status patients inflates released-label AUROC by 0.042 (0.010 to 0.078) and balanced accuracy by 0.040 (0.016 to 0.068) for logistic regression.

**Revised verdict:** GO for submission as a short research article covering three resources, once the authors' declarations are completed and the MMIST authors have been contacted. The manuscript is in [`manuscript.md`](manuscript.md).

## 1. What was verified about the data

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| Benchmark version | MMIST-LUNG commit `430670ce` (2026-09-17). All 5 handover file hashes match. |
| Handover reproduction | **35/35** exploratory quantities reproduced from freshly downloaded bytes |
| Upstream source | GDC Data Release 46.0 (2026-08-10). All 1,365 IDs linked one-to-one. Cohort-by-prefix equals GDC project for 1,365/1,365 patients. |
| Death times, MMIST vs GDC | TCGA 399/399 identical. CPTAC 89 identical; one death removed upstream and one added. |
| Alternative releases | TCGA-CDR (1,026/1,026 linked) and LinkedOmics CPTAC (218 linked). GDC agrees with them on 365-day status for 1,070 of 1,071 jointly ascertainable patients. |
| Time origin | GDC `index_date` = Diagnosis for 1,363 patients and Sample Procurement for 2 (excluded in a sensitivity analysis) |
| Fold file | `folds.npy` reproduced exactly (1,365/1,365) by `StratifiedKFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)` on the released `vital_status_12` in the order sorted TCGA, then CPTAC in `diagnosis.csv` order. The folds are stratified on the audited label. |

## 2. How the released label was generated (deterministic)

| Cohort | Rule that reproduces `vital_status_12` exactly | Agreement |
|---|---|---|
| TCGA | 1 (survivor) if `days_to_death > 365` **or no death recorded** | 1,026/1,026 |
| CPTAC | 1 (survivor) if `days_to_death <= 365` **or no death recorded**. This is the rule printed in `encode-csv.ipynb`, cell 14. | 339/339 |

The CPTAC rule assigns the survivor label to patients who **died within a year**, and the early-death label to patients who died **after** a year. The exactly-day-365 TCGA death is consistent with the TCGA rule, so it is a boundary convention, not an error.

## 3. Agreement with source-derived 365-day status (GDC, primary definition)

| | All | TCGA | CPTAC |
|---|---|---|---|
| Patients | 1,365 | 1,026 | 339 |
| Status ascertainable | 1,154 | 894 | 260 |
| Source early deaths (≤365 d) | 160 | 134 | 26 |
| Released early-death labels | 196 | 134 | 62 |
| **Inconsistent among ascertainable** | **88 (7.6%; 95% Wilson CI 6.2–9.3)** | **0 (0.0%; 0.0–0.4)** | **88 (33.8%; 28.4–39.8)** |
| Source early deaths labelled survivor | 26 | 0 | 26 |
| Released early deaths that survived >365 d | 62 | 0 | 62 |
| Not ascertainable, released as survivor | 211 (15.5%) | 132 | 79 |

- **In CPTAC, the released early-death label has sensitivity 0 and positive predictive value 0** for true early death.
- **Why status is not ascertainable:**
  - censored before day 365: 168
  - vital status "Not Reported" with no follow-up: 27
  - TCGA "Dead" without a death date: 9
  - alive with no follow-up time: 6
  - negative death time: 1
- **The overall survival rate looks right only because errors offset.** Kaplan–Meier 12-month overall survival is 86.8% (84.7–88.5), close to the released 85.6%. By subgroup, CPTAC is 90.5% by KM versus 81.7% released, and CPTAC LUSC is 93.5% versus 76.2%.
- **The handover's "10 contradictions" are resolved.** All 10 CPTAC patients censored at day 365 or later in LinkedOmics have a later death in MMIST/GDC, so their 365-day status agrees. This is a follow-up update, not a record error.
- **The DSS label is also affected.** MMIST's `vital_status_dss` equals 1 for every CPTAC patient, including the 42 whose GDC cause of death is "Cancer Related". CPTAC therefore contributes no disease-specific events to the benchmark's DSS task. In TCGA, the DSS label agrees with TCGA-CDR for 202 of 207 DSS events.

## 4. Consequences for model evaluation

These models are surrogates for the benchmark, not its MLP/Transformer: L2 logistic regression and gradient boosting on the same 15 clinical features, in the released `folds.npy`, plus stage-only and prevalence comparators. The original pipeline could not be re-run: its config reads encoded CSVs from non-released paths, and the archived checkpoints belong to a gastric experiment.

### Mechanism: the labels reverse the apparent cohort risk (post-hoc)

| Ascertainable patients (n=1,154) | TCGA | CPTAC |
|---|---|---|
| Early-death rate, released labels | 15.0% | **23.8%** |
| Early-death rate, source-derived labels | 15.0% | **10.0%** |
| Mean predicted risk, logistic trained on released | 13.3% | 18.9% |
| Mean predicted risk, boosting trained on released | 12.2% | 17.7% |
| Mean predicted risk, logistic trained on source | 15.0% | 9.5% |
| Mean predicted risk, stage only | 14.3% | 14.3% |

The 15 clinical features identify the cohort perfectly (out-of-fold AUROC 1.000), so a model can learn the cohort-level ordering in its training labels. This explains why the fixed-score contrast below is near zero within each cohort but not when pooled, and why the stage-only model moves the other way.

Pooled AUROC can also be split by the cohorts of the case and control in each pair (`exp_a_auroc_decomposition.csv`, post-hoc). CPTAC-case, TCGA-control pairs are ordered well (concordance 0.773 released, 0.752 source), and the inverted labels double their share (25.1% vs 12.4%). A Kitagawa split attributes 78% of the pooled logistic gap (−0.034) to the change in pair mix and 22% to changes in concordance. For the stage-only model, 94% of its gap (+0.024) comes from concordance.

### Experiment A: identical predictions, different labels (pre-specified primary contrast)

Models were trained on released labels, as the benchmark does. Fold-averaged AUROC was computed on the 1,154 ascertainable patients. Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over patients, conditional on the fitted scores.

| Model | AUROC vs released | AUROC vs source | ΔAUROC (source − released) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logistic (primary)** | 0.634 | 0.600 | **−0.034 (−0.068 to −0.003)** |
| Gradient boosting | 0.624 | 0.604 | −0.021 (−0.055 to +0.013) |
| Stage only | 0.609 | 0.635 | +0.026 (−0.011 to +0.063) |

**This effect is small and fragile.** The logistic estimate is negative in every pooled analysis, but the interval is close to zero and crosses it in several:

| Sensitivity analysis (logistic) | ΔAUROC (95% CI) |
|---|---|
| Death on day 365 counted as survivor | −0.035 (−0.069 to −0.004) |
| TCGA-CDR + LinkedOmics labels | −0.033 (−0.062 to −0.004) |
| Consensus of source releases | −0.032 (−0.060 to −0.002) |
| Released fold indices in ascending-ID order (released code's order) | −0.042 (−0.077 to −0.008) |
| **Excluding flagged cases** | **−0.027 (−0.056 to +0.004)** |
| **New stratified fold split** | **−0.029 (−0.065 to +0.004)** |
| TCGA only | 0.000 (labels identical among ascertainable) |
| **CPTAC only (26 events)** | **+0.011 (−0.206 to +0.140), inconclusive** |

Balanced accuracy, the benchmark's metric, does not change detectably for logistic regression (−0.013; −0.043 to +0.017). Brier score is lower against source labels for every model, including the prevalence-only model (−0.022); that is driven largely by the change in event prevalence, so it is not evidence of model quality.

The fold alignment alone moved the primary estimate from −0.042 to −0.034 (see changelog item 8). That sensitivity is itself a reason for caution.

### Model comparison across label sets (post-hoc)

- **Within a label set, no model comparison is resolved.** Under released labels, stage-only minus logistic is −0.029 (−0.072 to +0.014). Under source labels it is +0.035 (−0.012 to +0.083).
- **The shift between label sets is resolved.** On the same 1,154 patients, switching labels shifts the stage-only-minus-logistic gap by **+0.060 (0.026 to 0.098)** and the stage-only-minus-boosting gap by +0.047 (0.001 to 0.092).

So the label set changes the relative standing of the 15-feature models and the stage-only comparator, but this study does not establish that either model is truly better.

### Experiment A2: train TCGA, test CPTAC (fixed scores)

- With logistic regression trained only on TCGA (labels consistent there), AUROC on 260 ascertainable CPTAC patients is **0.659 against source labels versus 0.490 against released labels** (Δ +0.169, 0.018 to 0.312).
- The sign is the reverse of Experiment A: a model that never saw the inverted labels is penalised by them.
- The result depends on the model. Gradient boosting shows no difference (+0.002; −0.146 to +0.153), and stage-only is +0.067 (−0.074 to +0.202).
- On the handover's LinkedOmics subset the logistic result is +0.269 (0.116 to 0.403), consistent with the handover.

### Experiment B: which labels the model is trained on

Repeated CV (50 × 5-fold). Ranges reflect split variability only.

| Training labels | AUROC on source labels, ascertainable | AUROC on released labels, all (benchmark lens) |
|---|---|---|
| B1 released, all patients (benchmark practice) | 0.586 | 0.625 |
| B2 released, ascertainable only | 0.584 | 0.620 |
| B3 source-derived | **0.647** | 0.556 |

Logistic regression shown; gradient boosting is similar (0.582 / 0.584 / 0.643).

Patient-level paired bootstrap in the released folds (post-hoc; conditional on fitted models), source-trained minus released-trained:

| Model | Judged by source labels | Judged by released labels |
|---|---|---|
| Logistic | **+0.049 (0.015 to 0.082)** | −0.073 (−0.116 to −0.032) |
| Gradient boosting | **+0.054 (0.018 to 0.087)** | −0.051 (−0.089 to −0.010) |

- **Training on source-derived labels improves true-label AUROC,** and the improvement is in every one of the 50 CV repeats. Within CPTAC, AUROC is 0.73 versus 0.56 for logistic regression.
- **The benchmark lens points the wrong way.** A correctly trained model looks worse when judged by released labels, so benchmark-driven model selection would reject it.
- **Dropping unascertainable patients barely matters** (B2 − B1: −0.002). The polarity inversion, not censoring, drives the effect.

### Experiment C: handling of unascertainable outcomes

For logistic regression trained on source labels (pooled AUROC):

| Method | Result |
|---|---|
| Complete case | 0.646 |
| IPCW (censoring Kaplan–Meier stratified by cohort; max weight 1.20; effective n 1,152) | 0.648 |
| Unknowns imputed as survivors | 0.641 |
| Unknowns imputed as deaths | 0.578 |
| Sharp bounds over every completion of the 211 unknowns | 0.468–0.734 |
| Harrell C-index on full OS follow-up | 0.622 |

Censoring handling changes the point estimate only modestly here. IPCW assumes censoring is independent of outcome within cohort; the wide bounds show what is at stake if it is not.

### Experiment D: controlled leakage (hypothetical configuration)

Adding `vital_status_dss` as a predictor raises released-label AUROC from 0.637 to 0.686 (logistic). Adding `days_to_last_fup` raises it to 0.910. **This does not show the authors used these fields.** The released config targets `vital_status_dss` and drops `vital_status_12`. The experiment only quantifies the risk if someone switched the target without editing the drop list.

### Falsification checks (all pass)

- The label-permutation null centres on 0.500.
- The prevalence model's fold-averaged AUROC is exactly 0.5.
- Flipping the released labels of CPTAC recorded deaths recovers the source status in 88/88 cases (plus 1 version-changed case).
- `folds.npy` regenerates exactly; no train/test overlap.

### Independent case study: I3LUNG

The same audit applied to I3LUNG (Zenodo 17535424, CC BY-NC 4.0):

- `OS_6` agrees with its OS time and event fields for **1,972/1,972** patients, and `OS_24` for 1,699/1,699.
- Patients censored before the horizon are left **missing** rather than labelled survivors.

The procedure does not raise false alarms, and correct practice exists in a comparable public resource. This is not external validation of any MMIST-LUNG model.

## 5. What is not claimed

- That the **published** MMIST-LUNG numbers (MLP 56.7, XGBoost 65.0 balanced accuracy) are wrong by a specific amount. Their pipeline was not re-run, and the surrogate results do not transfer directly.
- That GDC is clinical ground truth. Agreement across releases reflects a shared upstream freeze.
- That the 15-feature models are worse than stage alone, or the reverse.
- Any clinical utility, deployment readiness, or relevance to patients in Uganda or any other setting.
- That the inconsistency was intentional. The pattern is consistent with an encoding error in a notebook the authors describe as not meant to run, but this has not been confirmed with them.

## 6. Decision gates

| Gate | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Source | **PASS** | Open-access sources; hashes pinned; 100% linkage; time origin verified; the 10 LinkedOmics discrepancies reconciled |
| 2. Outcome | **PASS** | Three-state 365-day outcome; boundary conventions tested; unknowns characterised by reason |
| 3. Consequence | **CONDITIONAL** | Primary contrast small and fragile (−0.034; −0.068 to −0.003). The larger effects (training labels, cohort reversal, model-gap shift, pair decomposition) are post-hoc and need to be presented as such. |
| 4. Novelty | **CONDITIONAL** | No prior report in the repo's issues or the searches run. The search was not systematic. Adjacent work exists (Tadj 2026; Northcutt 2021; label-space mismatch 2026). |
| 5. ML rigour | **PASS** | Leakage guard in code; fold-internal preprocessing; strong conventional comparator; training and evaluation effects separated; fold alignment reconstructed |
| 6. Interpretation | **PASS** | Surrogate models declared; original numbers not re-attributed; hypothetical leakage quarantined; post-hoc analyses labelled |
| 7. Output | **PASS** | Pipeline, tests, figures, dashboard, provenance manifest |
| 8. Publication fit | **CONDITIONAL** | Best fit is a short communication or benchmark-audit paper. Journal scope and fees not yet verified. |

## 7. Publication assessment

**Yes, this looks publishable as a short, focused article, but acceptance cannot be predicted.** No numeric probability is offered.

- **Strongest publishable core:** the deterministic label reconstruction, the source linkage, and the decomposition showing how the inversion reaches model evaluation.
- **Best-fit article types:** a benchmark audit, data-quality report or short communication. A workshop paper is also realistic.
- **Not yet a full original research article:** it covers one benchmark, the pre-specified contrast is weak, and the stronger machine-learning effects are post-hoc.
- **No obvious Matters Arising route:** the target is an arXiv preprint and workshop paper rather than a journal article, so the audit needs to stand alone. This has not been checked with any journal.
- **Candidate venues to check, not yet verified for scope, article types or fees:** *JAMIA Open*, *BMC Medical Research Methodology*, *PLOS Digital Health*, *Patterns*, and data-curation or machine-learning-for-health workshops.
- **Timing risk:** the finding is simple to reproduce and the repository is public, so others could report it, or the authors could correct the labels. A preprint would establish a dated record.

## 8. Conditions for full GO, and next steps

1. **Responsible disclosure.** Isaac decides whether to open a GitHub issue or email the MMIST-LUNG authors with the rule reproduction. Recommended before submission; **not done**. Their reply could also settle which fold alignment and which 12-month configuration they ran.
2. **Systematic search.** Run PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar and Semantic Scholar searches with citation tracking of arXiv 2609.05202, and read Tadj et al. in full.
3. **Confirm the post-hoc findings.** Pre-specify the training-label and cohort-reversal analyses for any extension, and refit models inside the bootstrap so intervals include fitting uncertainty.
4. **For a full article rather than a correspondence:** extend the audit to at least two more public multi-cohort survival benchmarks (fallback B), or re-run the original MMIST pipeline (torch) to quantify the effect on the published numbers directly.
5. Confirm the institution's ethics requirements for secondary analysis of public data.
6. Choose a venue, then verify its scope, article type, word limits and fees from publisher pages.
